posts.author: l8rose
posts.body:
Right now, I'm playing Dead Maze. A free to play Zombie Survival MMORPG. It's a pretty standard game with fetch quets and the like but it's kind of fun. It's only in beta whih means I don't have as much to do in it as when I first started (just daily quests for me at this point and farming resources). It's also casual enough that it fits my schedule right now so I get my gaming fix in.

posts.author: Touchfuzzy
posts.body:
Tokyo Mirage Sessions ♯FE. By far one of the most underrated JRPGs ever made. The theme is light, fluffy, silly, and absurd. The mechanics are excellent, the dungeon design is superb, the use of the Wii U tablet actually feels like part of the game and not tacked on, and it doesn't try to be bigger than it is.
It feels like Persona-lite in a lot of ways that are not necessarily bad just different: Shorter game, less angst, more fluffiness, less stress (you get all the time you want to finish all the side stories, rather than Persona's "YOU HAVE ONLY SO MANY DAYS, WHICH SOCIAL LINKS WILL YOU DO!"). It's just a fun game to pick up and play.

posts.author: Tarq
posts.body:
I've been playing Ni No Kuni. Nope, not the new one, I'm behind the times.
Its a good game but it feels like it got a lot of overwhelmingly positive reviews from sheer fanboyism? The animation, not the style, but the lack of different frames makes it look terrible; its surprising Ghibli didn't revoke their names from it (well, I suppose they did choose to abstain, as a company, from the sequel).
And as a game its another sub-par performance from Level5 who we've seen do significantly better in the past; was it crossed lines due to working with Ghibli? Have their earlier staff moved on or moved into managment roles as they've grown? All I can say for certain is that there's a lot of silly mistakes that just didn't exist in earlier games when they were lean and couldn't afford to code junk.
...But I'm still gonna finish it. Probably. Like said, it is good. If you can turn a blind eye to the squandered potential. And if it gets a little more chalenging, maybe.

posts.author: Madam_Detective
posts.body:
Mega Man 10: I decided to go back and give MM10 another shot in the weekend. I didn't like the game when I tried it last year. My first pick was Commando Man, and his stage frustrated the hell out of me with those pits and sandstorms. I went for another robot master this time, forgot his name, but he shoots thunderclouds at you. Started on Friday night, by Saturday night, I have already beaten all 8 robot masters. I was quite surprised because as a kid, I would be able to take on 1 or 2, or 3 if I am lucky, robot masters in one day. And yet, I somehow managed to beat them all in one day. And this game was supposed to be harder.
I got to Wily stage 2, then call it done.
I do think it was hard, but mostly the stage design that frustrated me. This game and MM9 have more spike traps and pits than the other games combined, I think.
It's just... boring and uninspired. The game feels so desperately trying to get me killed. "OMG why don't you die? Please die. Here's a pit with enemies around to screw you over, now die!". Enemies were also kind of more "rapey", as they constantly rush you and throw your aim off. It's so annoying and hilarious to see my bullets barely pass by the enemies' hitbox by a small margin and miss, while Mega Man stands there looking like a  then get hit. This happens way too often. I don't think the older games were this bad. But at least this game toned it down a notch compared to 9. Some pits are irritatingly hard to jump over, not sure what the deal is, but sometimes I would fail to make the jump and die. And I don't know what the hell it is but sometimes, Mega Man would fail to jump even when I press jump. Wtf?
I had a little chat with a coworker about MM on Friday. He said he liked MM9 and since he never played any MM game before, he thought that all MM games are like that. I hated this game with a passion, lol. The whole game is filled with death traps, spike traps, and death pits. Not only that, but craps shoot out death pits, too. It's like a fan game gone bad. Mega Man X8 was criticized as uninspired for having too many spike traps, but this one is praised to heaven. What gives? Well, at least the conversation made me feel like jumping back into Mega Man again, even if it was just for a little bit.
Corpse Party Blood Drive: Playing chapter 5, when Yoshiki is being chased. This game is fine, but it lacks the charm that the first game had. The loading screens are very annoying and the lag makes some segments of the game worse. There's this part when I have to run away from a bunch of ghosts who are closing in on me. The game lags right at that moment when I need to bypass them and got killed. That swimming segment in the pool was even more frustrating. It was damn hard to see where I was swimming, and the water was confusing to navigate through. Not sure how well this game will be on PC. The two characters with superhuman power don't really appeal to me very well. Well, let's play this to the end.
Just found out that all the CP games are going to be on PC this year. Can't ever imagine Hysteric Birthday being localized!
I think the PSP's version, Repeated Fear is better than the current PC version, so not sure if they will put that one up as well.

P4AU: I think last night was the first time I actually raged at this game. Hard.
Spoiler
Was playing Score Attack mode, on normal, and I picked Narukami. Nothing really gave me much trouble, until the 7th stage, when I fought against Minazuki. All hell broke loose.
Every time I got hit with an attack, and this means any attack, I would get inflicted with fear status, and take more damage. And this dude already deal more damage than any other character. I noticed that my attack did significantly less damage to him than usual. So not only do I take more damage, I would have to do more damage to him to win. This was next to impossible. Why? Because every hit from him inflicts fear status, when he performs a combo, I end up taking a lot more damage from the later hits. Just getting caught in one combo of his caused me to lose almost half of my health bar. To add insult the injury, sometimes, my Persona will be disabled, which means I couldn't use burst to get out of the combo. That's not the end of it, though. His SP skills do 2-3 times more damage than mine or any other characters' SP skills. And if he does it while I am in the middle of attacking, well, there is no way to dodge in time. I feel like his furious action has longer invisible frames as well.
I don't know how it wasn't as obvious before. Maybe because I have only fought him in story mode, for one round, and he was not too bad. Maybe he got some sort of buff in this mode. But this entire fight screamed "bullshit" to me and I called it quit after trying for like 50 times in vain. He wasn't the final boss or anything. Just an enemy in the 7th stage. Freaking weird.
Golden Arena mode feels more like survival challenges. Having to conserve your health for about 5-6 battles is tedious. And leveling up another character is quite time consuming.
I might go back tomorrow to get some last trophies, just for fun. But I guess I'm mostly done with this game. I had fun, but that last fight gave me a headache.
Mighty No. 9: If this game wasn't free for PS+, I wouldn't have bothered with it. And... what a trainwreck it was.
Spoiler
Tried this game tonight. The first impression I got was how dark everything is. I was shocked when I first started the game. "Uh, what the hell? Why is everything so dark?" I had to quit to the main menu to be able to fix the gamma value (oh god, why?). When I entered the game again, my second impression was how pixelated the models were. I thought I was looking at a PSP game, not a PS3 game. Actually, MMHX and MMPU looks even better than this game. What the hell happened here? Eh, gameplay wise, not too awful, or so I thought.
My first stage was the icy-water stage. Shortly after the beginning, I have to get past this nasty spike traps, which was a pain because it was so hard to see anything in that area. This seems bad already. Oh dear lord, the ice physics... I made it to the boss, but couldn't beat it. OK. Why the  does standing next to some blocks of ice and have them falling down next to me cause me to be frozen? And if it takes more than 4-5 seconds to break out of the ice, why don't you have me take damage instead? There was no way I could have broken out of the ice in time before the boss attacks me again. It was already a frustrating fight trying to get away from his freezing beam or whatever while wrestling with the icy floor, why do you have get frozen just by standing next to some ice blocks?
Second stage: the burning facility. Man. Another exercise in frustration. I have these bastards in the background shooting balls of flame at me. I have to anticipate where they are going to land while dealing with enemies ahead of me. They seem to have big hitbox, too. Sometimes, there was no way to dodge because the screen is already filled up with plenty of s: enemies' flame balls, charging enemies on the ground, enemies spraying fire wave at me. And then there's this part where the giant buildings fall on me. Come on, developers. I know you're trying to be Nintendo-hard but this is some desperation you have.
Biggest joke of this game? the frame rate. The game constantly slows down or having freezing issues. This is obvious when moving to a new area or an area with many enemies ahead. Movement can also feel kind of clunky and unresponsive at times.
Overall: I deleted the game after almost 2 hour or so. Good riddance. Guess I'm finally going to unbox that PS4 this weekend.

What can make them hard is that when you get to learning combos, Dante, Zero and Strider all have pretty hard combos compared to most other characters. Whereas character like Sentinel or Wesker can just do simple stuff like LMHS > super jump > MMHS > super and do like 75% of somebody's life. Spider Man is def super hard to play as well, I just liked playing him cause he's cool and I like hitting people with web throws
Characters do have different HP. Most characters have around 900,000~1,000,000. Thor has the highest at 1,250,00 and Phoenix is the lowest at 375,000. Usually fast characters have low HP and slow characters have high HP. It's been a long time, so I can't remember how red health recovery works, but I think it stops recovering for a while if you call a character as an assist and they get hit. So if you use assists a lot, you might recover slower than the CPU.
Under Night will definitely feel slower overall than a game like Marvel since it doesn't have air-dashes or wave-dashing (cancelling dashes into more dashes). It's more a slow and calculated pace - people usually call it 'anime Street Fighter'. But it also has a mechanic called Reverse Chain. In a game like Marvel you can only do attacks in order - Light > Medium > Heavy - and you can't go the other way around. In Under Night, you can do chains in any order, so you can do stuff like Light > Medium > Heavy > Medium > Light. Usually you do this so you can do some big slow move, chain it back into a Light, recover very fast, then start doing big moves again.
It's a bit different from most other fighting games, so if you didn't know about that, the game might feel slower than intended. When you're using everything you can, I think it goes at a pretty good pace, not too slow but not too fast. If you want a fast character, you can always try playing Seth:

I'm playing Tactics Ogre: Knight of Lodis and SaGa Frontier. (Final Fantasy Tactics Advance I played a lot later though and it was more fun than Knight of Lodis, at least at first). As for SaGa Frontier, I did a lot of watching gameplay years back and I finally am able to play. Although the game looks formulaic (a lot of things reused between stories) it felt surprisingly fresh to play through myself.. I actually appreciate the ridiculous difficulty curves/misguiding a lot because it feels really nice to have an accidental unwinnable situation even if it is total nonsense. The story telling of SaGa Frontier is arguably the best I've seen from a mainstream developer with Asellus (and I haven't played any other stories in the game except Lute which was interesting, but I got so quickly into a dead end and there probably isn't much more to his route sadly.) posts.author: nilm
posts.body:
Up until a few weeks ago I was playing Escape from Tarkov like my life depended on the grind lol. It's a fantastic simulation game in so many ways, and the developers put so much time and effort into the giant maps and wide array of weapons. I feel like their dedication to their vision of this game goes beyond most AAA studios.
Unfortunately both their best quality is also their worst. In their attempts to create the perfect simulation, they neglected a few critical aspects that heavily impact user experience. Mainly the existence of a player-controlled flea market that skews progression as well as encourages real money traders to purchase hacks to farm the most valuable items. And depending on how much you bring into a game, if a single hacker is present it could mean the loss of hours and hours of work.
Their quest system is also absurd. Often prompting you to either complete boring retrieval tasks, or tasks that're heavily reliant on pure luck. No one wants to spend 30 minutes per attempt at a low-tier quest that ends 9/10 times with a player killing you before you can complete it. And with certain gear and upgrades locked behind these quests, it makes it feel that much worse when you spend all night grinding 1 quest and make virtually no progress because you were unlucky.
It's a pretty brutal game with a steep learning curve, and I couldn't honestly recommend it to anyone and feel good about myself at this point in it's development. But I have dumped 400+ hours into it, so take that as you will.
